key_terms: A planned exercise that injects one named failure and checks recovery against an independent observation.
Deliberately causing a specific failure, such as a process restart, in an owned workshop only.
A random marker the course launchers verify before acting, so experiments never touch unrelated containers or volumes.
Reading existing state after an unknown outcome to decide whether a further write is needed, instead of replaying blindly.

worked_examples.title: Diff two identity receipts
worked_examples.interpretation: Only the container changed, which is the expected signature of a replacement over retained volumes. The same image and rows show that state and software survived. After a plain resume the dictionary should be empty. Any change in rows is the failure the exercise is looking for, so it should be written down before anything is reinitialized.

worked_examples.title: Break one setting in a disposable copy
worked_examples.code:
cp -R work/hive work/hive-broken
cd work/hive-broken
bash run.sh verify-schema
worked_examples.interpretation: Change exactly one value in the copy, such as the metastore database name in conf/hive-site.xml, and record the typed failure that verify-schema or start produces. Changing several things at once makes the error impossible to attribute. The original project stays untouched, so recovery means deleting the copy, not repairing the reference.

evidence: A selected actual supported path with independent source/result/failure/lifecycle evidence; combined topologies and prepared native-server alternatives require separate acceptance and are not inferred from component tests.
